title: Error taxonomy vocabulary
description: Closed vocabulary of the machine-readable error taxonomy (M01-W03): the twelve error families, the stable family-prefixed error codes, severity levels, retry/recovery dispositions, reporting origins (components/trust boundaries), message-key grammar, and the bounded user-safe message shape. The taxonomy defines errors only — executable capabilities and command allowlists are a different contract (M01-W04). Code evolution follows the enum rules of urn:japp:schema:common:enum-token:v1: adding a code is a MINOR change; removing, renaming, or semantically reassigning a code is a MAJOR change; deprecated codes remain defined for the rest of their major version. Every code's authoritative metadata (message key, default user-safe message, severity, disposition, flags, diagnostic policy) lives in the canonical validated error catalog instance (see urn:japp:schema:error:catalog:v1); wire records serialize only the stable code and consumers derive metadata from the catalog, so contradictory caller-supplied metadata is unrepresentable.

errorFamily.title: Error family
errorFamily.description: The twelve required error families. Every error code belongs to exactly one family and is prefixed by it.

errorSeverity.title: Error severity
errorSeverity.description: Impact class of the condition. WARNING: degraded but safely continuing. ERROR: the operation failed or must pause. CRITICAL: integrity, safety, or governance is at risk and the workflow must stop.

retryDisposition.title: Retry/recovery disposition
retryDisposition.description: Safe recovery classification. SAFE_RETRY: transient; the same operation may be retried without user involvement. RETRY_AFTER_REMEDIATION: retry only after the named condition is fixed. PAUSE_FOR_USER: automation must pause and hand control to the user; no automatic retry. NO_RETRY_PROHIBITED: the action is prohibited and must never be retried by automation. NO_RETRY_TERMINAL: this attempt or decision is final; recovery requires a new, separately reviewed action.

errorOrigin.title: Error origin
errorOrigin.description: Reporting component or trust boundary (spec §5.4/§5.5): the desktop app, extension content script, extension service worker, native messaging host, local orchestrator, model runtime, platform adapter, public job-index service, or the verification harness that executes benchmark and gate runs.

messageKey.title: Stable localization/message key
messageKey.description: Deterministic key derived from the error code: the literal prefix error., the lowercase family, a dot, and the lowercase family-stripped code remainder (underscores preserved). Example: VALIDATION_TYPE_MISMATCH has key error.validation.type_mismatch. Keys are stable for the lifetime of their code.

userSafeMessage.title: User-safe message text
userSafeMessage.description: Bounded, plain, non-interpolated English text safe to show a user: no placeholder syntax, no HTML, no URLs, no filesystem paths, no stack traces, no secrets, and no raw untrusted content. The generator additionally lints every catalog message against these rules and fails closed on violations; this schema enforces bounds and the character shape.

errorCode.title: Stable error code
errorCode.description: Closed set of stable UPPER_SNAKE_CASE error codes, visibly namespaced by family prefix. The canonical catalog instance defines exactly one metadata entry per code; the generator fails closed if this enum and the catalog ever disagree. Adding a code is a MINOR change; removal, renaming, or semantic reassignment is a MAJOR change.
